label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
output:
Kristen,

You asked for the straight story, so here it is, and I’m not going to dance around it. It was my popcorn.

Saturday around 10:40 I put a bag in the break room microwave and hit the popcorn button. Then I walked out front. A customer needed a shear pin for his snowblower and it took longer than I figured, maybe six or seven minutes. By the time I got back it had done what it did. Store was cleared for about 25 minutes. The engine came from up on Hertel. No damage, just smoke and stink. One of the guys on it was Mikey Szymanski — I broke him in as a probie back in ’03, so he will never let me forget this. Thirty-one years on the job and my first alarm as a civilian is over a bag of butter popcorn. My wife said the van smelled like a burnt movie theater.

The September alarm was not me. That was the sensor in the paint aisle. I want that clear since Gary’s asking.

It’s on me, not the microwave. I feel bad about the Hendersons leaving a full cart — they’ll be back, they always are, but I still feel bad. And tell Denise I’ve got her coffee.

For the $175, your call: take it out of my check or I bring cash. I’d rather keep my Saturdays. I like the weekend crowd and I need the hours for heating oil. I know that’s Gary’s question, so I’m asking straight out.

Sorry for the trouble.

Walt
